subcategory: Understand the organisation and its context
implementation: Produce a documented Context Analysis (PESTLE/SWOT) identifying internal factors (culture, governance) and external factors (regulatory, market, threat environment).
references: Show me this document and confirm it was reviewed in the last 12 months.
minimumEvidence: Signed context document with review date. / Internal & External Issue Register

subcategory: Understand the needs of interested parties
implementation: Produce an Interested Party Register listing stakeholders (customers, regulators, staff, suppliers) and their requirements (GDPR, SLAs, audit rights).
references: Show me your interested party register and link each requirement to a control/procedure.
minimumEvidence: Interested Party Register mapped to controls/SoA. / Needs & Expectations Register

subcategory: Determine the scope of the ISMS
implementation: Produce a written ISMS Scope Statement defining in-scope business units, locations, assets, and explicit justifications for any exclusions.
references: Is this scope realistic? Are any high-risk areas excluded without justification?
minimumEvidence: Approved ISMS Scope Statement document.

implementation: Demonstrate all ISMS processes are interconnected (risk assessment -> SoA -> controls -> monitoring -> review).
references: Auditor checks gaps between documented processes and actual operational practice.
minimumEvidence: ISMS Process Map / Framework Document.

implementation: Top management engagement, resource provisioning, policy approval, and strategic alignment.
references: Auditor interviews top management on ISMS objectives and recent audit findings.
minimumEvidence: Management Review minutes, approved ISMS budget, signed ISMS policy, board agenda items.

implementation: Top-level policy stating CIA commitment, regulatory compliance, risk management, and continual improvement. Must be communicated and annually reviewed.
references: Auditor checks version control, distribution records, and tests staff awareness.
minimumEvidence: Signed security policy, version history, staff distribution log, onboarding records.

implementation: Assign ISMS owner, CISO, DPO, asset owners, process owners, and incident response team roles.
references: Auditor asks key role holders to explain their specific ISMS responsibilities.
minimumEvidence: Documented RACI matrix, role definition documents, appended job descriptions.

subcategory: Actions to address risks and opportunities (General)
implementation: Produce a Risk & Opportunity Register for ISMS management (e.g., key role vacant, cloud migration).
references: Auditor checks that this register exists, is maintained, and has mitigation actions.
minimumEvidence: ISMS Risk & Opportunity Register with target dates.

implementation: Establish repeatable risk assessment methodology (likelihood/impact scales, acceptance threshold) and perform asset-based risk assessment.
references: Auditor samples 5-10 risks and verifies the methodology was applied correctly.
minimumEvidence: Risk Assessment Methodology doc, Risk Register with inherent/residual scores and sign-offs.

implementation: Formulate Risk Treatment Plan (RTP) and Statement of Applicability (SoA) covering all 93 Annex A controls.
references: Auditor checks every applicable control in SoA has a corresponding implementation record.
minimumEvidence: Signed Risk Treatment Plan (RTP), Statement of Applicability (SoA) signed by risk owners.

implementation: Establish SMART security objectives with clear owners, metrics, baselines, and targets.
references: How do you measure this? What is the current result?
minimumEvidence: Documented Security Objectives tracker with baseline and target metrics.

implementation: Formal change management process for structural/ISMS process changes (scope, standards, org updates).
references: Auditor asks about a recent major change and verifies it followed formal ISMS change control.
minimumEvidence: ISMS Change Request forms, impact assessments, approval records.

implementation: Determine and provide necessary resources (headcount, tooling, budget, external support).
references: Was the ISMS budget approved? What was spent last year?
minimumEvidence: Approved ISMS budget line, headcount plan, tooling procurement records, consultant contracts.

implementation: Define required competencies for ISMS roles and ensure personnel possess qualifications/training.
references: Auditor asks for competence records for key ISMS roles.
minimumEvidence: Competence Matrix, training certificates (CISM, Lead Implementer), CVs, personal development plans.

implementation: Ensure all staff understand policy, their role, and consequences of non-compliance.
references: Auditor spot-checks 3-5 staff (including non-IT) on security policy knowledge.
minimumEvidence: Annual training completion logs (100%), phishing simulation results, onboarding induction records.

implementation: Establish internal and external communications plan (what, when, with whom, how).
references: Show evidence of the last security communication sent to all staff.
minimumEvidence: Communications Plan, email broadcast records, intranet post logs, meeting minutes.

implementation: Control ISMS documentation (creation, review, approval, distribution, retention, access).
references: Auditor verifies Master Document Register matches documents actually in active use.
minimumEvidence: Document Register / Master List with version history, ownership, and defined retention periods.

implementation: Execute processes required to meet information security requirements and risk treatments.
references: Auditor traces sample operational events (access request, scan, incident) through documented process.
minimumEvidence: Operational logs, process execution records, outsourced process oversight logs.

implementation: Conduct formal risk assessments at planned intervals or following major changes.
references: When was the last risk assessment? What changed vs. previous assessment?
minimumEvidence: Updated Risk Assessment reports with timestamps, scope, and management sign-off.

implementation: Implement the Risk Treatment Plan and collect operational proof for all applicable SoA controls.
references: Auditor picks 10 SoA controls and requests live implementation evidence.
minimumEvidence: Configuration screenshots, policy docs, pen test reports, execution logs.

implementation: Establish KPIs and produce security performance reports at least annually / quarterly.
references: Auditor asks for the most recent metrics report and what management decisions it informed.
minimumEvidence: Security KPI / Metrics Report (MFA %, patch speed, phishing click %, incident count).

implementation: Conduct internal audits at planned intervals covering all clauses and SoA controls over 2-3 years.
references: Are internal auditors independent and competent? Are nonconformities tracked to closure?
minimumEvidence: Annual Internal Audit Programme, Audit Reports, Corrective Action Log.

implementation: Top management reviews ISMS performance at least annually against mandatory inputs.
references: Auditor reviews last 2 Management Review minutes to ensure all mandatory standard inputs were addressed.
minimumEvidence: Management Review Minutes with decisions, resource allocations, and assigned actions.

implementation: Continually improve the suitability, adequacy, and effectiveness of the ISMS.
references: Show me an improvement made in the last 12 months and how you verified it was effective.
minimumEvidence: Continual Improvement Register, effectiveness verification logs.

implementation: Re-evaluate nonconformities, perform root cause analysis, execute corrective action, and verify effectiveness.
references: Auditor checks closure evidence and root cause analysis for prior findings.
minimumEvidence: Nonconformity and Corrective Action Log with root cause analysis (5-Whys) and follow-up reviews.
